data.gender_notes: Josias is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Josias is derived from the Hebrew name Yošiyāhū (יוֹשִיעָהוּ), which means 'God heals' or 'Jehovah heals'. This name is mentioned in the Old Testament, specifically in the books of 2 Chronicles and 2 Kings, where Josias is depicted as a king of Judah who led a religious reform and restored the temple. The name Josias carries the meaning “God heals” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Josias usually hope their child will grow to embody god heals and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of healing and renewal.
data.etymology: Josias belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God heals.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Josias total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_hebrew.name: יֹשִׁיָּה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: יֹשִׁיָּה הוא שם שמשמעותו 'אלוהים תומך ומושיע'. השם נגזר מהשורש י-ש-ע, שפירושו 'להושיע' או 'להציל', ומ-אלוהים, שפירושו 'אלוהים'. השם יֹשִׁיָּה מוזכר במקרא כמלך יהודה, שהיה ידוע בצדקתו ובהשבתו של עם יהודה לתורת ה'.

in_greek.name: Ἰωσίας
in_greek.long_meaning: Ἰωσίας (Iōsias) σημαίνει 'Θεός ὑποστηρίζει καὶ σώζει', προερχόμενο ἀπὸ τὴν ἑβραϊκὴ λέξη 'יֹשִׁיָּה' (Yōshīyāh). Ὁ Ἰωσίας ἦταν βασιλεὺς τῆς Ἰουδαίας, γνωστὸς γιὰ τὴν δικαιοσύνη του καὶ τὴν ἐπιστροφὴ τοῦ λαοῦ στὴν ἀληθινή λατρεία.

in_latin.name: Josias
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Josias significat 'Deus supportat et salvat'. Etymologia nominis Josias provenit ex hebraico 'יֹשִׁיָּה' (Yōshīyāh), quod componitur ex 'Deus' et 'salvare'. Josias fuit rex Iudaeae, qui propter suam iustitiam et restaurationem populi ad veram Dei culturam notus est.

in_english.name: Josias
in_english.long_meaning: The name Josias originates from the Hebrew 'יֹשִׁיָּה' (Yōshīyāh), meaning 'God supports and saves'. It is derived from the roots 'y-sh-' (to save) and 'El' (God). Josias was a king of Judah, known for his righteousness and for leading his people back to the worship of the one true God. The name signifies divine support and salvation, reflecting a strong spiritual heritage.

data.cultural_impact: Josias holds cultural significance for his role as a pivotal figure in Jewish history, leading a religious and social renaissance during his reign. His efforts to restore the temple and reintroduce the traditional Jewish practices influenced the way Judaism was practiced and passed down through generations, shaping Jewish cultural identity. The name "Josias" itself became a reminder of this important period in history.
data.spiritual_significance: For Christians, the name Josias holds deep spiritual significance, as it is a reminder of God's healing power and grace. The name serves as a constant reminder to those who bear it that they are in God's hands and that he has the power to heal, restore, and revive not only their physical bodies, but also their souls and spirits. It can be a source of comfort, encouragement, and strength in times of need, as well as a reminder to strive for spiritual growth and restoration in one's own life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Josias symbolizes divine support and guidance in leadership and reform. Named after the biblical king who sought to purify the temple, Josias represents dedication to spiritual renewal.

biblical_reference.note: Josias was a king of Judah who reigned from 640 to 609 BCE.

historical_references.reference: Josias was a Judean king, the son of Amon, who reigned from 640 to 609 BCE. He initiated a religious reform, destroying the idols and high places in the temple and ordering the Law of Moses to be read in the temple every Sabbath day. This marked the beginning of the Deuteronomic reform, which aimed to centralize worship in Jerusalem and to enforce the Law.
historical_references.context: Judean king, religious reform, Deuteronomic reform, destruction of idols, Law of Moses

historical_references.reference: Josiah was a king of Israel who reigned from approximately 810 to 783 BCE. He was a godly king who did what was right in the eyes of the Lord. He began to restore the temple of the Lord and to repair the damages caused by previous kings. He also removed the idols from the temple and reinstated the Levites to their positions, allowing them to lead the worship of the Lord.
historical_references.context: Israelite king, godly king, temple restoration, idols removal, Levites restoration

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Josias is of Hebrew origin, meaning 'God is healer' or 'supported by Yahweh'. In the Bible, Josias is a king of Judah who, according to the Second Book of Chronicles, was responsible for religious reforms in Judah. This biblical figure has found modern relevance in various contexts. In pop culture, Josias appears as a character in several books and television shows. For instance, in the historical fiction novel 'The King's Secret' by Jillian Davidson, Josias is a major character. In fan fiction communities, Josias is a popular name for original characters in various fandoms. The name is also given to newborn boys in the United States and other English-speaking countries and is therefore seen as a contemporary given name. Josias has a rich history and continues to be a relevant name in modern times, with applications across various forms of media and personal naming practices.
